The critic's finding: DRE-7107: the relay's new "move into In Progress" trigger reads a one-off wearing `agent:planner` as an epic activation, so it would send the planner and not a build, and no criterion tests it.. What the re-plan changed: The second reviewer sent this plan back with five findings. All five are answered in this revision. No cards were added or removed. Six existing cards were rewritten, and the plan document was rewritten to match.

**1. A one-off wearing the planner's label would have been sent to the planner instead of being built — FIXED.**
Cards that come out of Planning can carry the planner's label without being epics. After the switch, the relay would have read that label on a card entering In Progress as the CEO approving an epic. The planner would then have moved the card back to Planning, and nothing would have been built. The relay card (DRE-7107) now checks whether such a card is really an epic: does it have children, or an epic stamp. It already does this today when a card enters Todo. A real epic is still approved the old way. A one-off is built. New tests cover the one-off being promoted, the build run's own move, and what happens when the check cannot reach Linear.

**2. The same defect reached the sweep, the switch's test and the proof — FIXED.**
- When the sweep re-fires a card that never started, it now always sends a build, never the planner (DRE-7108).
- The switch card's test (DRE-7120) now promotes a one-off wearing the planner's label alongside the ordinary cases.
- The proof (DRE-7132) now follows exactly that kind of card. The operator files the clean-up card at the end wearing the label on purpose and walks it to Done (DRE-7131). The proof then confirms it got exactly one build and no planner run.

**3. The switch waits for the relay to be merged, not for it to be live — FIXED, by stating the delay as accepted.**
We looked at holding the switch until the relay release is live. No build card can see that release, and putting a person's check in front of the switch would split this plan into two epics. So the switch card (DRE-7120) and the plan's risk section now say plainly what happens if the switch lands first: each promoted card starts up to about 30 minutes late, starts exactly once, and the cap and guards are unaffected. That lasts until our release train ships the relay, normally within an hour. The switch card's test covers that path. The operator card records whether the gap ever actually opened, and which cards it touched.

**4. A build held for a free runner could have been started twice — FIXED.**
When no runner is free, the console holds a build and posts a "held" note on the card. After the switch, the sweep would have re-fired that card after 15 minutes, and a busy afternoon could have doubled every held build. The sweep card (DRE-7108) now leaves a card alone while that note is the newest one and less than seven hours old. The runner-line card (DRE-7117) now commits to posting the same note for a card held in In Progress, and both cards test it.

**5. Possible overlap with other epics in flight — FIXED: checked, and there is none.**
The reviewer could see only the other epics' titles, so it flagged the overlap as unconfirmed. We read the file lists of every card in the five epics it named. Every file they share with this plan belongs to a card that is already Done. Their open cards are proof and operator records that touch nothing of ours. The result is now written into the plan.

Which gets to the one thing left for you: once the second review passes it, approve this epic by moving only the epic to In Progress. The cards are promoted in order from there. The review is being run again by the pipeline, on its own, as round 2 — nothing here is yours to decide, and the epic stays in Planning. If it sends the plan back again with a finding this revision did not settle, or the plan keeps growing new gaps, the epic parks in Triage with needs-human for an operator.

The critic's finding: DRE-7120: the "accepted delay" rests on a false premise: the relay live today does not ignore a `Queued → In Progress` move on a card wearing `agent:planner`, it sends that card to the planner.. What the re-plan changed: The second reviewer sent this plan back with five findings, and this revision fixes all five. No cards were added or removed. Four cards were rewritten (DRE-7110, DRE-7120, DRE-7131, DRE-7132), and the plan document was updated to match.

**1. The "accepted delay" rested on a false premise — FIXED.**
The last revision said that if the switch went live before the new relay, a promoted card would just start up to 30 minutes late. That holds for most cards, but not for a one-off carrying the planner's label. The relay we run today reads that label alone as the CEO approving an epic. So it would send the planner instead of a build, the card would go back to Planning, and it could loop. The reviewer was right. We checked the relay's code and it does exactly that.

We did not paper over it. We closed it on the pipeline side. The planner's dispatch guard (DRE-7110) now checks every planner dispatch it receives for a card entering In Progress. If the card is a one-off with no sub-cards and has not started, the guard plans nothing, moves nothing, and starts one build itself. That card starts within minutes, once, and never goes back to Planning. The guard reaches the pipeline's release channel before the switch can, because the switch card now waits for it.

**2. The switch card's wording and test did not match what the relay really does — FIXED.**
The switch card (DRE-7120) now describes both cases plainly. A card without the label is ignored by the old relay and re-sent by the sweep, up to about 30 minutes late. A one-off with the label is sent to the planner and handed back as a build by the guard. Its test used to fake a relay that does nothing. It now fakes the old relay's real answer for both kinds of card, and checks that each card gets exactly one build and never goes to Planning. The plan document's risk section says the same thing. It also names the one fallback left: if Linear cannot be read at all, the card can go back through Planning once before it is promoted again.

**3. The proof's walk card was the one card the gap would have bounced — FIXED.**
The operator card (DRE-7131) now files the walk card only after confirming that the new relay is live, and records both times. So the walk card meets the relay this epic built, not the gap. If it still goes anywhere unexpected, the operator records that as a finding and does not fix it by hand.

**4. The proof asked for a console reading the proof run cannot make — FIXED.**
The proof run has no way into the production console. So the proof card (DRE-7132) now checks the console's release from our release tags, which it can read. The board check — no Todo column, and the same In Progress cards as Linear — moves to the operator card as a reading taken in a single minute. The proof reads that record back. The proof card was already blocked on the operator card, so it waits for that reading.

**5. The proof did not say how it would read the label at the moment of the move — FIXED.**
The proof card now names the exact Linear query, which includes label changes, and the rule for reading it. The label counts as present at the move when the card wears it now and nothing added it after the move. The record quotes the query's answer and checks it against the operator's record.

The pipeline is re-running the second review on its own, so nothing here needs you yet. Once that review passes the plan, approve it by moving only this epic to In Progress. The cards are promoted in order from there. The review is being run again by the pipeline, on its own, as round 3 — nothing here is yours to decide, and the epic stays in Planning. If it sends the plan back again with a finding this revision did not settle, or the plan keeps growing new gaps, the epic parks in Triage with needs-human for an operator.

What the re-plan changed: The second reviewer sent this plan back with five findings. All five are fixed. No cards were added or removed, and the plan still has 28 cards, ending with the same proof card.

**What changed, in short.** The plan had a gap at its very end. The final cleanup check scans the relay (the small service that turns a card move into a build). Two kinds of leftover mention of the old "Todo" lane would have made that check fail: the relay's messages and internal checks still named it, and its copy of the pipeline's lane list still listed it. No card was assigned to remove either. One existing card now owns that work. I also tightened one card so the planner's run leaves approved epics alone, and added rebase notes to two cards.

**Finding by finding, in the reviewer's order:**

1. **The final cleanup check would fail on relay text nobody was assigned to change — FIXED.** The card that cleans up the console backend's descriptions now also cleans up the relay. It removes every remaining mention of the old lane from the relay's messages, log labels and lane checks. The one rule that starts a build on entry to the start lane stays in place, now driven by the shared setting instead of a typed name. The card was renamed to say so, resized from small to medium, and set to wait for the earlier relay cards and for the pipeline's retirement card. The final cleanup card now says plainly that it only checks the relay and never edits it.

2. **The relay text in detail, and the release it needs — FIXED.** Same fix as finding 1. The card lists each kind of leftover the reviewer named (the "is in Todo" message, the "move the card back to Todo" texts, the lane comparisons, and the guard's wording), with a count taken today. It also says the change does nothing until the relay is released, and that the operator confirms that release before the old lane is deleted.

3. **The relay's lane list only drops "Todo" after a second refresh, and nothing ordered it — FIXED.** The same card now does that second refresh itself. It takes the pipeline's settings from the approved channel once the retirement card has reached it, or confirms the automatic refresh already landed, and it stops and says so if the retirement isn't there yet. The final cleanup card now waits on it, and stops and says so if the refresh is missing. The operator card now checks that the released relay contains this card and records three values from it: the start lane, where buildable work goes, and a lane list with no "Todo". The lane is not deleted until that is recorded. The proof card compares the relay against those recorded values.

4. **Widening the build-start check would have made the planner's run treat an approved epic as a build card — FIXED.** The planner's run uses the same check. After the change it would have started checking approved epics, and could have relabeled one or sent it back to Planning. The card now says an epic, or a planner-owned card that isn't marked as a single piece of work, is left alone exactly as today. It adds a test that runs the check the way the planner's run does, against an approved epic, and shows nothing is touched. The planner's workflow file itself does not change. The card that owns that file only updates a comment to match.

5. **Two cards will need a rebase behind work from another epic — FIXED (it was a note, not a blocker).** Two pull requests from another epic are in review and touch one file each that two of our cards also edit. Both will merge first. Each of our two cards now carries a note: start from the file as it stands then, change only the sentences about the old lane, and keep the other epic's changes. The cost is a rebase, not a conflict over meaning.

Nothing else in the plan changed. The automated checks pass on the revised cards: every card is valid, and the proof card is still last and waits on every other card. When it is settled, clear needs-human, then move the epic from Triage to Planning, where the planner re-plans it on a fresh attempt and both critics read it again before it goes anywhere else.
